sovereign_country.strategic_role: 西欧核心消费市场、高客单价品牌合规与本土清关

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Single-Origin Green Arabica Coffee Bean Container Distribution

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (continental codified tradition with a dual ordering of judicial and administrative courts)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: EU-Vietnam Free Trade Agreement (EVFTA), in force 1 August 2020
EU-Colombia-Peru-Ecuador Free Trade Agreement, provisionally applied since 2013 for Colombia and Peru and 2017 for Ecuador
EU-Central America Association Agreement, provisionally applied since 2013 and covering Guatemala, Honduras, Costa Rica, Nicaragua, El Salvador and Panama
EU-Kenya Economic Partnership Agreement, in force 1 July 2024
Agreement between the French Republic and the Federative Republic of Brazil for the Avoidance of Double Taxation, signed 1971 and amended by subsequent protocols

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Articles L.561-1 et seq. and L.561-2-2 of the French Monetary and Financial Code (Code monétaire et financier) governing the AML/CFT framework and the UBO Register; Loi n° 2016-1691 of 9 December 2016 (Sapin II Law); Décret n° 2018-284 of 18 April 2018 on UBO declarations; Loi n° 2020-1508 of 3 December 2020 transposing EU AMLD5; UBO Register (Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs) technically administered by INPI since 1 January 2021 with filing via the Guichet Unique of formalités

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified true copy of the passport or national identity document of each UBO and each natural-person shareholder holding directly or indirectly 25% or more of the share capital or voting rights
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary, civil registrar or consular authority in the UBO's country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille where the origin state is a 1961 Hague Convention member; otherwise consular legalization at the French Embassy of the origin state

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Original proof of residential address (utility bill or bank statement dated within the last three months) for each UBO and each director
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Utility provider or credit institution of the UBO's country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Sworn translation into French plus Hague Apostille or consular legalization depending on the jurisdiction of issuance

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of corporate existence or official registry extract (equivalent of a Kbis extract) for any corporate shareholder, accompanied by its articles of association and a shareholders' register excerpt identifying the ultimate controlling persons
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Company registry of the corporate shareholder's jurisdiction of incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization, followed by sworn translation into French

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Original notarized power of attorney allowing the French formation agent or a designated avocat to execute the incorporation filings where any shareholder or statutory officer signs remotely
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the jurisdiction where the foreign signatory is located
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization plus sworn French translation

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory pre-incorporation screening of all UBOs, proposed directors, managing officers and beneficial shareholders against: (i) the EU consolidated financial sanctions list (EU Council implementing regulations), (ii) the UN Security Council consolidated list, (iii) the French national asset-freezing list maintained by the Direction Générale des Douanes et Droits Indirects and the Direction du Trésor, (iv) the OFAC SDN and supplementary screening lists to the extent that USD SWIFT payments or US-dollar collections from documentary letter of credit settlement are anticipated, and (v) the domestic French list of politically exposed persons under FATF Recommendation 12. The screening shall follow the TRACFIN guidance and the regime of Article L.561-5 of the Monetary and Financial Code; any positive hit triggers enhanced due diligence under Article L.561-10-2, a risk-based escalation to the designated AML compliance officer, and where warranted a declaration of suspicion (déclaration de soupçon) to TRACFIN under Article L.561-15. The transaction profile of ISIC 4631 specialty green coffee bean container distribution is rated low-risk by the French banking AML tiering, however, the use of documentary letters of credit and cross-border wire transfers remains subject to full customer due diligence at the receiving French credit institution and to country-of-origin risk scoring for the coffee-exporting jurisdiction.
ubo_and_aml_profiling.ubo_disclosure_details: The French UBO Register is not open to the general public. Access is restricted to judicial authorities, TRACFIN, customs and tax administrations, and AML/CFT-regulated entities performing statutory due diligence. Access may also be granted to any person demonstrating a legitimate interest on a case-by-case basis in accordance with the jurisprudence of the European Court of Justice (Cases C-37/20 and C-601/20 of 22 November 2022) and the resulting French Conseil d'État practice.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Guichet Unique des Formalités des Entreprises operated by INPI (Institut National de la Propriété Industrielle) at https://formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr, with name availability verification conducted against the Registre National du Commerce et des Sociétés (RNCS) and the INPI trademark database at https://data.inpi.fr
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The corporate name (dénomination sociale) of a French SAS must be stated in Latin-alphabet characters. French-language legal and linguistic rules require that where a foreign-language or non-Latin-script name is used, a transliteration into Latin script and, where necessary, a French-language description be provided to avoid confusion in trade. The name must comply with the constitutional requirement that French is the language of the Republic and with the Loi Toubon (Law n° 94-66if 4 August 1994) in consumer-facing documentary materials. The statutes must append the legal form 'SAS' in all official acts, and the chosen name must be capable of distinguishing the company from existing names in the RNCS and from prior trademarks, without inducing confusion contrary to Article L.711-3 of the French Intellectual Property Code.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Banque or Établissement de crédit - reserved to licensed credit institutions under the Monetary and Financial Code
Assurance or Réassurance - reserved to undertakings authorized under the French Insurance Code
Notaire, Avocat, Huissier, Commissaire de justice - protected by professional monopolies and ministerial appointment
France, République, Préfecture, Ministère, État - imply a connection with the State and require prior ministerial authorization where permitted
Chambre de commerce - reserved to chambers operating under French administrative law

Crédit, Fiduciaire, Bourse, Investissement, Fonds - regulated activity-related tokens requiring prior approval from the Prudential Supervision Authority (ACPR) or the AMF where the intended business falls within regulated financial services
Commerce extérieur and Douane - sensitive import-related tokens that may require additional explanatory documentation but are not absolutely prohibited for a bona fide and licensed import company
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: French law does not provide a stand-alone name reservation certificate for an SAS; name availability is verified at the moment of filing the incorporation dossier through the Guichet Unique. Where the INPI or the Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce refuses or rejects the name, the incorporator may, within 15 days of the formal rejection: (i) resubmit a fully corrected dossier with a revised denomination and no material defects; (ii) file a preferential administrative appeal (recours gracieux) addressed to the INPI presenting comparative evidence of non-confusion and the results of RNCS and trademark database searches; or (iii) where the rejection concerns an RCS opposition based on a prior identical or confusingly similar name, petition the Président du Tribunal de Commerce statuant en référé for an order declaring the availability of the proposed name. A refusal issued by the INPI in its capacity as operator of the Guichet Unique may ultimately be challenged before the Administrative Court of Paris within two months of the decision. The 30-day validity window refers to the recommended documentary shelf-life of the preliminary non-opposition attestation and availability search used by advisers prior to filing.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permissible for a green-coffee import trading and container distribution company. Under Article L.123-11-2 of the French Commercial Code, the registered office (siège social) may be domiciled at a prefecture-authorized commercial domiciliation company (société de domiciliation) for a maximum period of five years, provided the domiciliary delivers a valid domiciliation certificate enabling receipt of legal correspondence and statutory notices. This structure is accepted for the SAS provided no physical industrial activity is conducted at the registered seat, which is consistent with the wholesale import and B2B distribution of specialty green coffee beans under ISIC 4631. In practice, the opening of the bank account, the issuance of documentary letters of credit, customs broker instructions and French VAT registration records may require the company to evidence additional physical commercial substance at a place other than the registered seat, such as a leased warehouse or a customs-bonded facility.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low to moderate, quantified at approximately 5-8% within the first 24 months of operation. Unannounced inspections may be conducted by the Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce to verify the existence of the registered seat, by the Direction Générale des Douanes et Droits Indirects for customs and indirect tax verification at the place where the goods are cleared, and by social and tax inspectors upon an audit trigger. The likelihood increases if the company claims significant VAT refunds, presents pricing anomalies in customs valuation, or maintains a passive registered seat without any demonstrable trade substance.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Pre-incorporation restructuring advice and drafting of the French SAS Articles of Association (statuts) by a licensed French avocat, including UBO structure review and AML verification memo
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark of €250-€500 per hour for corporate transactional work; fixed-fee engagement accepted for a standard SAS

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Name availability search and trademark conflict verification at the RNCS, the commercial registry database and the INPI trademark register
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: INPI and registered legal-intelligence search providers
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Official INPI data access charges and third-party registry search benchmark fees

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Publication of the mandatory incorporation legal notice (formation notice) in a licensed Journal d'Annonces Légales (JAL)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory requirement; market tariff grid of licensed JAL publishers for an SAS incorporation notice

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Single incorporation filing through the Guichet Unique and registration of the company in the Registre National du Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) before the competent Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: INPI and Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Official fixed greffe tariff (tarif des greffiers) applicable to the formation of a Société par Actions Simplifiée, including administrative legal costs

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Sworn translation into French of foreign UBO documents, corporate shareholder registries extracts, notarized powers of attorney and residence proofs by a court-certified translator (traducteur assermenté)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Expert judiciaire listed with a French Cour d'Appel
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Official per-page rate of approximately €40-€80 per 250-word page

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Apostille and consular legalization batch for approximately four origin-country documents supporting the identity and corporate existence of foreign UBOs and shareholders
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the document origin state and/or consular post of the French Embassy
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Official consular legalization and apostille fee schedules, typically €45-€75 per document

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Authorized commercial domiciliation of the registered office (siège social) for a 12-month term using a prefecture-approved société de domiciliation
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Agréée domiciliation company authorized by the relevant French prefecture
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark of €60-€100 per month for B2B trading company domiciliation

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Opening of the blocked share-capital deposit account (compte bloqué) at a French credit institution pending registration of the SAS, applicable where initial cash capital exceeds zero
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: French credit institution (e.g., Bpifrance partner banks, commercial banks)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Bank tariff grid for blocked capital accounts, typically a flat fee of €100-€250

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: UBO register declaration preparation and filing coordination with the INPI for the identification of the beneficial owners at the 25% ownership threshold
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: French avocat or legal compliance service provider
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark; official transmission of the UBO declaration is bundled within the Greffe/INPI single-filing tariff

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: French Commercial Code (Code de commerce), Articles L. 227-1 to L. 227-33 (Société par Actions Simplifiée), Article L. 210-2 (formation, lawful object and capital), Articles R. 123-1 et seq. (RCS registration); implementing rules via Decree No. 2023-407 (Guichet Unique / INPI single window).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: INPI Guichet Unique (formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr) as the single electronic filing window; Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce of the registered-office jurisdiction for RCS registration and Kbis issuance.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Dossier unique de création d'entreprise (online M0/company creation form) filed via the INPI Guichet Unique, accompanied by signed Articles of Association (Statuts), bank capital deposit certificate, legal announcement certificate, and Declaration of Beneficial Ownership (DBE).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum or maximum capital for an SAS (Article L. 227-2); capital is freely fixed in the Articles (market practice: EUR 1,000-EUR 15,000). Cash subscriptions must be deposited before RCS registration in a blocked account (compte bloqué) opened with a French bank or the Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations; the bank's attestation de dépôt des fonds is filed with the Guichet Unique and funds are released only upon presentation of the Kbis. In-kind contributions must be fully paid up at incorporation and must be valued by a commissaire aux apports unless the statutory exemption applies. No escrow beyond the blocked deposit account is required.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, by unanimous written consent of the founders constituting the first governance act of the Société par Actions Simplifiée: 1. The Articles of Association are hereby approved and adopted, and the company is constituted under Articles L. 227-1 et seq. of the French Commercial Code. 2. The founders irrevocably subscribe to and pay up the share capital under the terms of the Articles. 3. The registered office is fixed at the address stated in the Articles; the President is authorized to open branch offices. 4. [Name] is appointed President with full corporate authority to represent the company and to execute banking, administrative, commercial, and licensing formalities. 5. All required publications and filings are expressly authorized. This minute is final and complete, and no further resolutions are required.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and execution of the Articles of Association (Statuts)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Founders/legal counsel; notarial deed only if real-property contributions are made or if a notary is voluntarily chosen
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Statuts in French containing all mandatory clauses: corporate name, legal form (SAS), registered-office address, corporate purpose (import and wholesale distribution of specialty green coffee beans), duration (maximum 99 years), share capital and number/classes of shares, identity of all shareholders, rights attached to shares, rules for transfer of shares, appointment and powers of the President, decision-making procedures, and fiscal year-end. Each shareholder signs the final version (electronic signature accepted). Attach a valuation report for any in-kind contribution subject to statutory audit. Execute a separate nomination letter or keep the President's appointment in the Statuts.
required_dossiers: Signed Statuts (original)
Identity documents of natural-person shareholders
Corporate shareholders: Kbis or equivalent foreign register extract
Commissaire aux apports valuation report (if in-kind contributions are made)
Power of attorney for the signatory, if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Guichet Unique or the Greffe refuses the Statuts for missing mandatory clauses, file a rectificative application with amended Statuts (acte rectificatif) before the deadline stated in the query; no court action is required if the defect is cured within the regularization period.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Opening of a blocked capital-deposit account and issuance of the bank deposit certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial bank in France (or Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations if no bank accepts the deposit)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The founder(s) open a temporary account in the name of the company in formation ('société en formation') and transfer the cash subscriptions stated in the Statuts. The bank verifies AML/KYC data, freezes the funds, and issues the attestation de dépôt des fonds / certificat de dépôt. Upon completion of registration, the bank releases the capital to the company against presentation of the Kbis extract.
required_dossiers: Bylaws or draft Statuts (to evidence legal capacity of the company in formation)
Identity documents of beneficial shareholders
Feasible business/account-opening questionnaire and source-of-funds declaration
Bank deposit certificate (attestation de dépôt des fonds)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank refuses the deposit on AML grounds, provide the requested economic-ownership and source-of-funds documentation; alternatively deposit with Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations or another credit institution. No regulatory penalty applies if the certificate is obtained before filing; if deposit was made but certificate is delayed, submit the filing once the certificate is received.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publication of the legal formation notice in a Journal d'Annonces Légales (JAL)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: A news publication approved to carry legal announcements in the département of the registered office (JAL)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the 'avis de constitution' to the JAL containing legally required mentions: corporate name, legal form, registered-office address, corporate purpose, amount of share capital, share split, duration, identity and address of the President, and the RCS registry town. Pay the publication fee. Obtain an attested copy of the publication (justificatif de parution) to be attached to the incorporation dossier.
required_dossiers: Signed Statuts (sent to JAL editor)
Completed announcement form with all legal mandatory mentions
Payment receipt for publication fees
Attested copy of the published announcement (certificat de parution)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the JAL rejects the announcement for missing or inconsistent mentions, correct the text and republish on the next publication day; the company must ensure the publication date is prior to submission of the Guichet Unique dossier, otherwise the statute of limitations for third-party challenge starts late. Re-publication charges are the sole remedy cost.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Electronic submission of the full incorporation dossier via the INPI Guichet Unique
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Institut National de la Propriété Industrielle (INPI) – single window at formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Log on to the Guichet Unique portal, select 'création d'une société', choose the legal form 'SAS' and NAF/APE activity code 4637Z (wholesale of coffee, tea, cocoa and spices; corresponding to ISIC 4631). Complete the dynamic M0-equivalent form (corporate name, address, capital, shareholders, President, controllers, beneficial owners, activity details), upload the Statuts, bank deposit certificate, legal announcement certificate, DBE declaration, identity documents, and proof of the registered-office address, then pay the EUR 84.94 (approx. USD 92) official registration fee online. Receive an electronic acknowledgement of the completeness check.
required_dossiers: Completed online M0/creation form data
Signed Statuts (PDF)
Attestation de dépôt des fonds from the bank
Certificat de parution of the legal announcement
Declaration of Beneficial Ownership (DBE) – allowed to be filed separately within 15 days
Identity documents of shareholders and President
Proof of authorized use of registered-office address (bail, domiciliation contract, or ownership deed)
Proof of payment of the INPI filing fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Guichet Unique returns the dossier for incompleteness or irregularity, the filer receives a 'dossier non conforme' notification with a curative deadline (generally 10-15 days); resubmit the corrected documents within the deadline to preserve the filing date. If the deadline is missed, refile as a new application with a new fee; in case of unlawful refusal, appeal to the supervising judge (juge du contrôle) of the Commercial Court within 15 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: RCS registration, allocation of SIREN/SIRET numbers and issuance of Kbis
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce of the registered-office jurisdiction (on behalf of the Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After the Guichet Unique validates the dossier, the Greffe registers the company in the RCS, allocates the SIREN (9-digit) and SIRET (14-digit) identifiers and the APE/NAF code, and issues the Extrait Kbis, which is the certified proof of legal existence. The President verifies the registered data, the legal form, the corporate purpose, and the registered office address; once the Kbis is received, the blocked capital is released by the bank. The Kbis is used for all subsequent administrative, banking, customs and licensing procedures.
required_dossiers: Guichet Unique validated dossier number (no new annexes normally required)
If queried by the Greffe: original signed Statuts in print
If queried: up-to-date identity documents and DBE
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Greffe issues a refusal to register ('refus d'immatriculation'), the company may regularize the defect and re-present the dossier, or file a summary petition (requête) before the president of the Commercial Court when the refusal is wrongful. Registration can also be obtained by court order in urgent cases.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-registration governance formalities: URSSAF, DREETS, DGCCRF, tax office and physical premises clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: URSSAF, INSEE, Direction Régionale de l'Économie, de l'Emploi, du Travail et des Solidarités (DREETS), Direction Générale de la Concurrence, de la Consommation et de la Répression des Fraudes (DGCCRF), and Service des Impôts des Entreprises (SIE)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After receipt of the Kbis: open a permanent corporate bank account; declare the company as an employer with URSSAF (in Paris, via RSI/URSSAF) before any hire; verify INSEE codes and correct any APE miscoding; if the company physically stores packaged or bulk green coffee in a warehouse, file the prior food-business/warehouse declaration required by Regulation (EC) No 852/2004 with DGCCRF; register the establishment with DREETS for workplace health and safety records; ensure the registered office is signposted and that fire extinguishers, first aid and emergency signage are in place; open the tax file with the local SIE; formalize the President's governance acts in the corporate register (procès-verbal de décisions and registers).
required_dossiers: Extrait Kbis
Lease contract or domiciliation agreement for registered office/warehouse
President's identity and proof of address
DGCCRF prior warehouse/food-business declaration form (if storage activity exceeds de minimis)
URSSAF employer registration form
Fire-safety compliance checklist and building occupancy documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If URSSAF or DREETS issue late-declaration penalties, submit the missing declarations with a reasoned request for leniency (demande gracieuse); if DGCCRF considers the company an undeclared food establishment, regularize by completing the prior declaration which is immediately effective for wholesale-only activities; no operating license penalty applies for green-coffee trading per se because no statutory license is required in the French classification.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Direction Générale de la Concurrence, de la Consommation et de la Répression des Fraudes (DGCCRF) – for food-business/warehouse prior declaration; Direction Régionale de l'Environnement, de l'Aménagement et du Logement (DREAL) – for environmental classifications
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No special operating license is required in France for wholesale distribution of green (unroasted) specialty Arabica coffee beans under ISIC 4631/NAF 4637Z; the activity only requires the standard RCS business registration, plus, if applicable, a simple prior déclaration d'activité as a food-warehousing operator under Regulation (EC) No 852/2004, and compliance with general commercial, occupational and customs rules.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Direction Régionale de l'Environnement, de l'Aménagement et du Logement (DREAL)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt – no dedicated EIA is required because the import and wholesale storage of green coffee in commercial bags is not an ICPE (Installation Classée pour la Protection de l'Environnement) activity; a simple declaration under ICPE rubrique 1510 (entrepôt couvert) becomes necessary only if the covered warehouse exceeds 500 m³ of storage volume; roasting or processing would trigger a different ICPE evaluation (rubrique 2415) which is outside the current scope.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: N/A for green-coffee trading and storage. If later upgraded to include cleaning, roasting, or grinding, the facility must respect the emissions and wastewater threshold values of the ICPE order applicable to rubrique 2415 (particulate matter, VOCs and odours), plus Code de l'environnement Articles R. 512-1 et seq.; for the current pure wholesale activity, no specific discharge or VOC permit is needed.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety: the office portion must comply with the general fire safety requirements of the Code du travail (accessible exit routes, illuminated emergency exits, portable extinguishers, and fire detection if premises size requires); public-access areas, if any, trigger ERP (Établissement Recevant du Public) classification and approval by the commission de sécurité. Warehouse clearance: for sites above 500 m³, a déclaration to the DREAL under ICPE rubrique 1510 plus a fire-safety assessment are required. Occupational clearance: registration with DREETS, display of health-and-safety notices, emergency first-aid kit, compliance with the Code du travail on air quality, lighting and worker protection, and, where applicable, the social and economic committee (CSE) formalities for staff above 11 employees.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP) — impots.gouv.fr
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Foreign entities must obtain a French VAT number (numéro de TVA) and a corporate tax identifier (Numéro SIREN) by registering with the DGFiP through the Guichet Unique (formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr). Non-established entities without an EU seat of business must file a specific registration form (Cerfa n° 15787) with the Service des Impôts des Entreprises (SIE) territorialement compétent, and, if not established within the EU, must appoint a fiscal representative (représentant fiscal) subject to DGFiP approval. The application requires standard corporate documentation, proof of non-resident legal existence, and identification of the actual place of management. The resulting numéro de TVA intracommunautaire (EU VAT ID) is required for intra-EU trade and export zero-rating documentation.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: An SAS is mandatorily taxed as a separate capital company under French corporate income tax (Impôt sur les Sociétés, IS) and has no US-style check-the-box election. The principal statutory elections available are: (i) election for fiscal integration ('intégration fiscale') where the SAS is at least 95%-owned by a French parent, allowing group tax consolidation; (ii) election of the parent-subsidiary regime ('régime des sociétés mères et filiales') to benefit from the 95% exemption on qualifying dividend distributions; and (iii) election to file on a non-calendar year-end subject to tax authority approval. Hybrid mismatch elections are not permitted; French anti-hybrid rules under EU ATAD are mandatory.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (Taxe sur la Valeur Ajoutée, TVA)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No registration threshold for non-established foreign suppliers: a taxable person not established in France must register for French VAT from the first taxable transaction physically performed in France unless the reverse charge rule or the EU One-Stop-Shop (OSS) regime applies. For domestic French small businesses, the franchise threshold is EUR 85,000 annual turnover for sales of goods and EUR 34,400 for services, but this is not available to foreign-established persons.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: France is rolling out a mandatory electronic invoicing and e-reporting reform ('Réforme Facturation Électronique'). B2B e-invoicing becomes compulsory from 1 September 2026 for large enterprises and from 1 September 2027 for all VAT-liable businesses, including SAS entities. All B2B invoices must be issued in a structured format (Factur-X, UBL, or CII) and transmitted through a certified dematerialization platform (PDP) or the public portal (Portail Public de Facturation, PPF). E-reporting of all domestic B2C and export transaction data is simultaneously mandated to DGFiP. Currently, France does not operate a real-time pre-clearance or digital stamping system; clearance occurs through electronic data interchange with customs (DELTA) and tax validation via the invoicing platforms.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: The export of specialty green coffee beans from France to an EU-external destination qualifies for zero-rated VAT (Art. 262-I-1° CGI) when the seller proves (i) dispatch of the goods after a binding sale, (ii) the goods physically leave French and EU territory, and (iii) export documentation is accepted by French customs. For intra-EU deliveries, zero-rating applies if the customer is a VAT-registered trader in another Member State and the goods are transported to that State (Art. 262-I-2°). The exporter must retain transport contracts, commercial invoices, customs export declarations (DAU/AES), and proof of exit or arrival. Green coffee beans imported from third countries into France are chargeable with import VAT at 20%, which must be paid upon customs clearance unless placed under a suspension arrangement such as customs warehousing.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Déclaration d'Exportation / DAU / Automated Export System record evidencing exit from the EU)
Bill of Lading or Shipping Company Transport Document evidencing physical delivery to a non-EU country
Inward Remittance Certificate / Bank SWIFT Credit Advice evidencing receipt of export proceeds
Commercial Invoice issued in the name of the foreign buyer
Contract of Sale and Incoterms clause
Certificate of Origin and Phytosanitary Certificate (for green coffee beans)
VAT identification and export watch request (Art. 262 register)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: DGFiP systematically audits export zero-rating claims and may reconstruct the transaction if the export file is incomplete, inaccurate, or inconsistent. If the required proof is not produced within the audit window, the tax administration issues an assessment for the unpaid VAT at 20% plus interest (0.2% per month), increased by a 40% penalty for bad faith (mauvaise foi) and 80% for deliberate fraud under Arts. 1727 to 1729 CGI. False export documentation triggers criminal customs penalties under Arts. 414-415 French Customs Code, including forfeiture of goods, fines of up to three times the evaded amount, and imprisonment for smuggling. The standard assessment limitation period is three years, extended to six years in the presence of fraudulent activity or unexplained omissions, and the exporter must retain supporting records for at least ten years for definitive proof.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque de France (Bank of France, Eurosystem member), with foreign-exchange policy and external-financial-regulation implementation shared with the Direction Generale du Tresor (French Treasury, Ministry of Economy and Finance); prudential licensing and supervision of resident credit institutions and payment services is exercised by the ACPR (Autorite de Controle Prudentiel et de Resolution). Legal basis: Code Monetaire et Financier (CMF), Arts. L.151-1 et seq. and R.152-1 et seq.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Euro is fully convertible; France maintains no exchange-control permit regime for current-account or capital-account movements. Current-account payments (green-coffee import settlements, commissions, freight, insurance) and capital flows between France and EU/EEA residents are unrestricted; transactions with non-EU parties enjoy the same freedom, subject only to (i) EU/UN financial sanctions (e.g., Reg. (EU) 833/2014 and 36/2012 as amended) and (ii) mandatory balance-of-payments statistical reporting by the receiving/remitting bank (per transaction >= EUR 2,000; monthly aggregate >= EUR 10,000; CMF Art. R.152-3). Profit remittance is free; no statutory dividend withholding applies to EU/EEA corporate shareholders holding >=5% under the Parent-Subsidiary Directive and CGI Art. 145; non-EU shareholders are subject to the applicable double-tax-treaty rate on dividends. No IEF/FDI prior approval (CMF Arts. L.151-3 et seq.) is triggered for a French non-regulated coffee wholesale importer classified under ISIC 4631.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Since EU capital liberalisation, France imposes no surrender of export proceeds, no mandatory conversion ratio, and no statutory repatriation deadline. Export receipts in USD or other convertible currencies may be retained indefinitely in a foreign-currency compte de devises at a French or EU bank without central-bank approval. Banks must file balance-of-payments statistics with Banque de France for each cross-border flow >= EUR 2,000 or when the monthly aggregate exceeds EUR 10,000 (CMF R.152-3). Physical transportation of cash or bearer negotiable instruments of EUR 10,000 or more into/out of France requires a customs declaration under EU Regulation 2018/1672.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational EUR current account; optional blocked capital-deposit escrow (compte bloque) for pre-incorporation funds
Operational EUR current account with documentary LC and USD correspondent clearing
Operational EUR account; multi-currency and trade-finance line
Operational EUR account; strong credit documentaire (LC) and correspondent-banking network

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: BPCE - Groupe Banque Populaire / Caisse d'Epargne
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational EUR account; regional group with variable trade-finance appetite

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low-to-Medium as sole treasury rail; Medium as auxiliary settlement. ACPR-licensed French or EU-passported EMIs/payment institutions under PSD2 (e.g., Qonto, Shine; ManSA for Francophone-Africa corridors) may execute SEPA, outbound SWIFT MT103 and basic EUR/USD conversion, but cannot issue documentary credits (MT700), handle UCP 600 presentations, or provide high-value USD nostro clearing. Third-country (offshore) EMIs without an ACPR authorisation or EU passport cannot lawfully provide payment services to an FR SAS (CMF Arts. L.521-1 and L.572-1); their use as primary treasury rail is legally constrained and operationally inadvisable.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: For first onboarding with trade-finance needs, French Tier-1 banks generally require the physical appearance of the SAS President (legal representative) and every 25%+ UBO at a branch. Videoconference e-KYC is accepted for a simple operational account, but a documentary LC, a SWIFT-corporate access, or an inbound capital transfer exceeding EUR 100,000 will trigger a face-to-face compliance interview or require a notarised, apostilled power of attorney (procuration) naming a France-resident mandate holder. Non-resident officers must supply certified translations of identity documents and proof of address; the bank cross-checks the RCS beneficial-owner register (Declaration des Beneficiaires Effectifs) filed at the Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unverifiable source of non-resident shareholder capital in subscription (source-of-wealth documentation gap)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed statutes and souscription d'actions; 3-12 months bank statements of the transferring shareholder; tax residence certificates; board minutes and corporate authorisations; structured source-of-wealth letter; prior financial statements if the shareholder is a company.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Payment-routing mismatch: invoice/beneficiary differs from the actual wire recipient (tri-party or cooperative settlement for green coffee)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed CIF/FOB coffee sales contract; proforma invoice and payment instruction letter from the seller; agency/intermediary agreement; KYC pass of the ultimate beneficiary; UBO chain of the origin-country cooperative; bills of lading, inspection certificate and phytosanitary certificate covering the same shipment; management board resolution approving the disbursement.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Trade-based money-laundering flags: invoice price or weight materially divergent from ICE 'C' benchmark or quality certificates
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete trade file: contract quoting ICE Arabica 'C' differentials; SGS/Intertek quality-and-weight report; packing list; bill of lading; freight and insurance proofs; customs entry and TARIC liquidation documents; audited reconciliation of invoiced value against benchmark plus premium/deduction clauses.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions/high-risk-jurisdiction exposure: beneficiary, bank or beneficial owner appears on EU/UN sanctions lists, or transshipment touches prohibited territory
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: RCS beneficial-owner declaration; sanctions screening certificates (EU/UN/OFAC) for all parties; negative-news diligence; certificate of origin and ICO certificate of origin for the coffee; anti-sanctions warranty in the import contract; counsel attestation confirming absence of IEF/CMF L.151-3 sensitivity.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Approval of annual accounts and allocation of result
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months after the financial year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late approval may support court proceedings and management liability; no automatic annual strike-off applies solely for late approval.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Deposit of annual accounts and, where applicable, management report and auditor report
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Commercial court registry through the French one-stop business formalities portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month after approval of the accounts, or within two months after approval when filed electronically
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Court injunction and daily penalty payments may apply; failure to deposit may also result in a fifth-class fine of up to approximately EUR 1,500, increased for repeat violations, and may contribute to administrative RCS removal procedures.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate income tax return Form 2065 and financial schedules
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Generally within three months after the financial year-end; for a calendar-year company, electronically by the second business day after 1 May
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing generally triggers a 10% surcharge and late-payment interest at the statutory monthly rate; higher penalties may apply for intentional non-compliance or tax fraud.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual VAT return and balance payment, where the SAS is under the normal annual VAT regime
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Generally during the second business day after 1 May following the relevant calendar year; monthly or quarterly filings apply under other VAT regimes
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late or omitted VAT filing may trigger a 10% surcharge, late-payment interest, estimated assessment, and additional penalties for inaccurate or fraudulent reporting.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Beneficial owner information update following a change
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Commercial court registry through the French one-stop business formalities portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 days after a change affecting the beneficial owner or reported beneficial ownership information; no routine annual confirmation is required
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Court injunctions, fines, restrictions on registry formalities, and potential criminal liability may apply for inaccurate or missing beneficial owner information.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A statutory auditor is generally mandatory for an SAS exceeding at least two of the following thresholds at the financial year-end: EUR 5 million total balance sheet, EUR 10 million net annual turnover excluding tax, and 50 average employees. Additional group-level and shareholder-request triggers may apply.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: French generally accepted accounting principles under the French Accounting Standards Authority framework (Plan Comptable Général). IFRS may apply to qualifying consolidated accounts and is not generally mandatory for an unlisted standalone SAS.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: France has no routine annual beneficial owner confirmation filing. Share transfers must be recorded in the securities accounts and transfer register, and the beneficial owner declaration must be updated within 30 days if the transfer changes beneficial ownership or previously reported information.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of shareholders and securities accounts
Register of shareholder or sole-shareholder decisions
Register of decisions of the president and other corporate bodies where applicable
Beneficial owner documentation and evidence supporting the filed declaration

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: Approximately USD 650-2,000 per year for commercial domiciliation or registered-office services
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: Approximately USD 3,000-12,000 per year, depending on turnover, transaction volume, group reporting, inventory controls, and audit complexity

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% standard corporate income tax rate. A qualifying small enterprise may apply a 15% rate to the first EUR 42,500 of taxable profit, subject to French SME eligibility conditions, including generally turnover not exceeding EUR 10 million, fully paid-up capital, and at least 75% ownership by individuals or qualifying entities.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No general tax holiday applies to a French SAS conducting ordinary green coffee import and distribution. The 15% SME rate may apply to the first EUR 42,500 of taxable profit. Research and development tax credit, innovation tax credit, and geographically targeted incentives are available only where their statutory conditions are independently satisfied. French participation exemption may substantially reduce taxation of qualifying dividends received by a French parent, generally through a 95% exemption mechanism.
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: Unlimited carryforward, subject to the annual utilization cap of EUR 1 million plus 50% of taxable profit exceeding EUR 1 million. Carryback is generally limited to the preceding financial year and capped at the lower of the preceding year's profit or EUR 1 million.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 2065-SD, corporate income tax return, with the applicable 2058-A-SD through 2058-F-SD tax computation schedules and 2059-A-SD through 2059-G-SD balance-sheet and tax analysis schedules; filed electronically through the French tax administration's EDI-TDFC channel or the impots.gouv.fr professional account where available.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual corporate income tax return; quarterly corporate income tax instalments are generally payable on 15 March, 15 June, 15 September, and 15 December, with a final balance payment generally due on the 15th day of the fourth month following the financial year-end.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For a financial year ending on 31 December, the annual return is generally due by the second business day following 1 May of the following year. For a financial year ending on another date, filing is generally due within three months after the closing date. Electronic filing rules and exceptional annual extensions must be verified for the relevant tax year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name, SIREN number, registered office, financial year dates, tax office, principal activity, and legal form.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use the French SAS's own SIREN, French registered office, and actual accounting period. Identify the foreign parent separately; do not substitute the parent's tax identification number for the SAS's SIREN.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Corporate income tax liability, normal or simplified accounting regime, and electronic filing identification.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident-owned SAS remains a French resident corporate taxpayer on its own taxable profits. Select the French corporate income tax regime applicable to the SAS, not the parent's residence-country regime.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable profit or tax loss transferred from the detailed tax computation schedules.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include French-source trading income, including import and distribution margins, and make statutory tax adjustments for non-deductible expenses, provisions, depreciation, financing costs, and related-party charges.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Add-backs and deductions reconciling book result to taxable result.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Disclose deductions for eligible expenses only where incurred in the SAS's interest, properly documented, and consistent with French transfer-pricing and deductibility rules.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Current-year loss, carried-forward losses used, and remaining losses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply the EUR 1 million plus 50% annual utilization limitation. Maintain supporting schedules for all carried-forward losses and any ownership or activity changes that may restrict their use.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross and net fixed assets, additions, disposals, depreciation, and tax bases.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Record French assets and depreciation of the SAS. Imported inventory is not a fixed asset; coffee inventory must be valued under French accounting and tax rules, with purchase, freight, customs, insurance, and directly attributable costs properly allocated.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Corporate income tax, credits, instalments, balance payable, and overpayment.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Credit only legally available French tax credits. Foreign taxes are not automatically creditable against French corporate income tax and require applicable treaty or domestic-law authority.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Transactions requiring supplementary forms, including transfer-pricing documentation, withholding tax, tax consolidation, and tax-credit information.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report cross-border purchases, financing, royalties, management fees, guarantees, and other dealings with the foreign group at arm's length and reconcile them to the general ledger and customs records.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Summary of the group's legal structure, controlled transactions, methods, and documentation status where the statutory EUR 50 million threshold or another trigger applies.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: File only where a statutory trigger applies, but retain contemporaneous support for all material controlled transactions even where Form 2257 is not mandatory.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Foreign tax credits and related foreign-source income where applicable.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Do not claim a foreign tax credit for a parent or sister company. Claim only taxes legally borne by the SAS and supported by certificates and the relevant treaty or French-law provision.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late or non-filing generally attracts a 10% surcharge, potentially increased to 40% for deliberate non-compliance and 80% in cases of fraudulent conduct or abuse. Late-payment interest is generally 0.20% per month, subject to statutory rules. Failure to file electronically may trigger a separate surcharge. Tax reassessments may also generate interest, penalties, and collection costs.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 2572-SD, corporate income tax balance and instalment payment mechanism, generally processed electronically through the impots.gouv.fr professional account or linked electronic payment channel.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Quarterly instalments and one annual balance payment.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Instalments are generally payable on 15 March, 15 June, 15 September, and 15 December. The final balance is generally due on the 15th day of the fourth month following the year-end; a 31 December year-end generally produces a 15 May balance deadline.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Current-year instalment calculated by reference to the preceding year's corporate income tax, subject to statutory exceptions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Calculate instalments from the French SAS's own corporate income tax liability. The foreign parent's tax payments, losses, and credits are irrelevant.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Current-year corporate income tax less instalments and permitted credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Reconcile the balance to Form 2065 and retain payment confirmations, bank references, and tax-account statements.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Applicable exemption, first-year status, or reduced-payment condition.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Verify whether the SAS is in its first taxable period or qualifies for an exemption. Do not rely on the parent's start-up status or foreign tax payments.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late payment generally causes a 5% payment surcharge for tax debts, in addition to late-payment interest where applicable. Incorrect instalment calculations can produce collection action and interest. Persistent non-payment may result in formal notice, enforced collection, bank seizure, or director liability in exceptional cases of deliberate fraud or serious mismanagement.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: For dividends paid by a French SAS to a non-resident corporate shareholder, the domestic withholding rate is generally 25%, subject to exemptions and treaty relief. The EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive exemption may eliminate withholding where the statutory ownership, holding-period, subject-to-tax, beneficial-ownership, and anti-abuse conditions are satisfied. Dividends paid to a non-resident individual are generally subject to a different domestic regime, commonly 12.8%, before treaty analysis.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Determine the recipient's treaty residence, beneficial ownership, legal status, ownership percentage, holding period, limitation-on-benefits or principal-purpose requirements, and anti-abuse status. Obtain a current certificate of tax residence from the recipient's foreign tax authority. For French relief-at-source or refund procedures, use the applicable French forms, commonly Forms 5000-FR and 5001-FR for dividends, or the relevant treaty-specific form. Submit the forms to the recipient's tax authority for certification and provide them to the French payer or French tax office within the prescribed period. If relief at source is unavailable, withhold domestically and seek a refund supported by the certified residence form, payment evidence, dividend statement, and beneficial-owner documentation. Treaty relief is not available merely because the shareholder is incorporated in a treaty country.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: French domestic withholding on royalties and similar payments to non-residents is generally 25% under Article 182 B of the French Tax Code, subject to statutory exemptions, EU rules, and treaty limitations. Interest paid by a French company to a non-resident is generally not subject to ordinary French withholding tax, but exceptions may apply, including payments to residents of non-cooperative jurisdictions or arrangements affected by anti-abuse rules. Treaty rates vary by treaty and commonly range from 0% to 15% for interest and 0% to 10% for royalties. Payments to related parties must also satisfy arm's-length pricing, beneficial-ownership, deductibility, and anti-hybrid requirements.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Full transfer-pricing documentation is generally mandatory where the French entity or group meets a statutory EUR 150 million threshold based on turnover or gross assets, or where specified ownership, control, tax consolidation, or comparable group conditions apply. A simplified transfer-pricing declaration, Form 2257-SD, generally applies at a EUR 50 million threshold or where specified related-party or group conditions are met. Documentation may be required below these thresholds to defend the arm's-length nature of material transactions.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: France has no standalone regime using the terminology of a separate Economic Substance Regulations filing comparable to certain offshore jurisdictions. Nevertheless, French anti-abuse rules require genuine business purpose, real decision-making, appropriate personnel and assets, beneficial ownership, and consistency between contractual arrangements and actual conduct. The general anti-abuse rule, principal-purpose analysis, controlled foreign company rules, anti-hybrid rules, interest limitation rules, permanent-establishment principles, and beneficial-owner tests may deny treaty benefits or deductions for artificial arrangements. A French SAS importing and distributing coffee should maintain local commercial substance proportionate to its functions, including personnel or outsourced operational control, inventory management, customer and supplier contracts, customs capability, banking control, and board decision records.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Corporate income tax evasion and fraudulent accounting
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Concealing French sales, understating inventory or customs values, creating fictitious expenses, diverting sales to a foreign affiliate, maintaining dual books, or deliberately omitting taxable income.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Tax reassessment, late-payment interest, and penalties of up to 80% of the evaded tax in aggravated cases. Criminal tax fraud may carry up to five years' imprisonment and a EUR 500,000 fine, with higher penalties, including up to seven years' imprisonment and EUR 3 million, for aggravated or organized fraud cases, subject to statutory conditions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may incur criminal liability, tax-fraud liability, management-fault liability, and civil damages. Courts may order professional disqualification, confiscation, or publication measures. Travel restrictions are not automatic but may arise from judicial control, arrest warrants, or enforcement proceedings.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Overpricing coffee purchases from a related foreign supplier, underpricing sales to a foreign affiliate, charging unsupported management or royalty fees, using a non-arm's-length financing rate, or failing to produce required Local File, Master File, or transaction records.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Adjustment of taxable income, denial of deductions, withholding-tax consequences, and penalties for documentation failure. The documentation penalty may generally be at least EUR 10,000 and may reach the higher of 0.5% of the relevant controlled transactions or 5% of the reassessed profits or taxable income, subject to the applicable statutory provisions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may face civil liability where the conduct causes tax loss or insolvency and criminal liability where documentation is part of fraudulent concealment. A foreign parent does not automatically shield a director who knowingly approves abusive pricing.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Customs, import VAT, and origin fraud
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Misdeclaring coffee origin, tariff classification, customs value, quantity, importer of record, or preferential-origin status; using false commercial invoices; or circumventing import VAT and customs controls.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Recovery of customs duties and import VAT, customs penalties, seizure or forfeiture of goods, withdrawal of customs simplifications, and potentially criminal prosecution for customs fraud. Food, traceability, sanitary, and deforestation-related supply-chain breaches may generate additional administrative or criminal consequences depending on the conduct.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and customs representatives may be personally prosecuted for intentional customs fraud or false declarations. Civil recovery and asset seizure may follow. Travel restrictions or imprisonment depend on judicial proceedings and the seriousness of the offense.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Money laundering, terrorist financing, and beneficial-owner concealment
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Receiving unexplained third-party funds, disguising the beneficial owner, routing payments through opaque intermediaries, structuring transactions to avoid controls, or processing proceeds of crime through the SAS or its bank accounts.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Suspicious-transaction reporting, account blocking, asset freezing, confiscation, administrative enforcement, and criminal money-laundering penalties. Basic money laundering may carry up to five years' imprisonment and a EUR 375,000 fine, with aggravated cases carrying materially higher penalties, including up to ten years' imprisonment and a EUR 750,000 fine, subject to statutory conditions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly participate, facilitate, or negligently authorize the conduct may be criminally liable. Courts may order confiscation, professional bans, judicial control, and restrictions on movement. The SAS's limited liability does not protect intentional personal participation.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining a nominal French SAS with no genuine activity, employees, functions, inventory control, commercial risk, or decision-making while routing profits solely to obtain treaty, interest, royalty, or dividend benefits.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Denial of treaty benefits, application of domestic withholding, reassessment under the general anti-abuse rule, denial of deductions, interest, and penalties of up to 80% in cases of abuse or fraudulent conduct. A shell company is not unlawful solely because it has limited staff, but artificiality and abusive purpose create substantial exposure.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be liable for fraudulent abuse of rights, mismanagement, false corporate records, and creditor prejudice. The corporate veil may be disregarded in exceptional circumstances involving fraud, confusion of assets, or fictitious activity; imprisonment and travel restrictions require a separate judicial basis.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Illegal profit distribution and insolvency misconduct
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Distributing dividends without distributable profits, disguising dividends as service fees or shareholder loans, repaying shareholder debt while insolvent, or transferring assets to the foreign parent to prejudice creditors or the French tax authority.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Repayment of unlawful distributions, director liability for management faults, possible misuse-of-corporate-assets offenses, insolvency proceedings, clawback of suspect-period transactions, and criminal penalties where statutory elements are met.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may face civil restitution, contribution to insolvency liabilities, management bans, and criminal prosecution for misuse of company assets or bankruptcy offenses. Travel bans and imprisonment are possible only where ordered by a competent court under the applicable offense.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Failure to withhold, report, or remit cross-border tax
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Paying dividends, royalties, interest, or service fees without applying the correct French withholding, relying on an uncertified residence certificate, failing to verify beneficial ownership, or omitting required reporting.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Recovery of the unpaid withholding tax from the French payer, applicable interest, penalties, and possible denial of treaty relief. Deliberate concealment may escalate to tax-fraud proceedings.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The legal representative may be exposed to personal liability in cases of intentional or repeated failure, particularly where the company is used to defeat tax collection. Civil recovery is more common than imprisonment absent evidence of deliberate fraud.
